detaileddescription.para: After Installation of PDI step, PDI must be used in the application, that is written either in C/C++, Fortran or Pyhton.

sect2.title: PDI was installed in default location
sect2.para: The library and plugins should be found without any problem, but a good approach is to make sure that all environment variables are set correctly. To do this, there are 3 options:

listitem.para: source pdirun - sets up current environment variables
pdirun bash - creates new shell with environment variables set up
pdirun command - runs a command with all environment variables set up

sect2.para: To have the environment always prepared for using PDI, the first option (source pdirun) can be added to ~/.bash_profile file. After that, any new shell will have environment variables set up.

sect2.title: PDI was installed in custom location
sect2.para: To prepare environment in this case there are 3 options:

listitem.para: source PDI_path/share/pdi/env.bash - sets up current environment variables
PDI_path/bin/pdirun bash - creates new shell with environment variables set up
PDI_path/bin/pdirun command - runs a command with all environment variables set up

sect2.para: where PDI_path is the path where PDI was installed.

To have the environment always prepared for using PDI, the first option (source PDI_path/share/pdi/env.bash) can be added to ~/.bash_profile file. After that, any new shell will have environment variables set up.

sect1.title: Compilation of an application
sect1.para: If source files (of application that uses PDI) and specification tree file are ready, the compilation step can be made. For C make sure that source files that use PDI API are including pdi.h header file. For Fortran make sure that source files that use PDI API are using PDI module file (USE PDI).

sect1.title: Running an application
sect1.para: PDI is a shared library. That means that all environment variables must be set not only on compilation, but also when running the program.
Every used plugin in application needs to be found by PDI. It will search for plugins in 4 steps (it will use the first plugin found):

listitem.para: PDI_PLUGIN_PATH environment variable that is colon separated list with paths,
plugin_path subtree in specification tree: plugin_path,
Relative path of used PDI shared object libpdi.so,
LD_LIBRARY_PATH environment variable that is colon separated list.
